time_expectation: Designed so that a correct solution (sequence export, Bloch simulation of about 2e4 isochromats, reconstruction and checks) fits within the 60-minute session on a shared CPU without GPU.
acquisition: 2D single-slice multi-shot turbo (fast) spin echo at z = 0: 2 acquired shots, each one slice-selective 90 deg excitation followed by an echo train of 9 slice-selective refocusing pulses with one acquired phase-encoded echo after each refocusing pulse (18 acquired echoes in total)
flip_angle_definition: realized on-resonance flip angle 360 deg x |integral of the RF waveform (Hz) over time|; tolerance 2% of nominal; every RF pulse in the sequence is either an excitation (90 deg) or a refocusing (135 deg) pulse; the refocusing flip angle is fixed by SAR
slice_selection: every RF pulse is played with a z gradient on and no x or y gradient; the slice is centred at z = 0 (RF frequency offset 0)
echo_spacing: interval between the centres of consecutive refocusing pulses; constant within each train and at most 0.013 s
effective_echo_time_definition: from the centre of the excitation pulse of the shot that acquires ky = 0 to its ky = 0, kx = 0 ADC sample (sample index 9); tolerance 20 us
repetition_time_definition: interval between the centres of the excitation pulses of consecutive shots, identical for all shots including any non-acquired shots (tolerance 1 us)

sampling_contract.readout: one ADC per acquired echo with 18 samples whose k-space positions are kx = (i-9)/fov_m, i = 0..17, in chronological order (sample 9 at kx = 0); Pulseq sample times are delay + (i+0.5) x dwell; k-space positions follow the usual rule that each refocusing pulse inverts the accumulated gradient moment
sampling_contract.phase_encoding: each echo has one ky = (j-9)/fov_m with j in 0..17 (kz = 0 at the samples); every j acquired exactly once over the 18 acquired echoes; the assignment of lines to shots and echoes is free

echo_train_requirement: for an on-resonance test column of isochromats at x = y = 0 spread over z (as in the phantom), with any 0.35 s <= T1 <= 1.6 s and 0.045 s <= T2 <= 0.28 s, the phase of the kx = 0 sample of every echo of every acquired shot must lie within 15 deg of the circular mean phase of the echoes of that shot
shot_steady_state_requirement: for the same test columns, the kx = 0 magnitude of the first echo must agree within 1% across the 2 acquired shots
image_quality_requirement: for any object of the described kind, the magnitude image reconstructed from the measurement must have a mean magnitude in background voxels at least 2 voxels away from the object below 5% of the median magnitude in the reference region

phantom.content: x_m [18] and y_m [18] in-plane voxel-centre coordinates (x_m[9] = y_m[9] = 0), z_offsets_m [105], and 18x18 [y,x] maps density, T1_s, T2_s, B0_Hz, labels
phantom.isochromat_model: the object is the outer product of the in-plane grid and z_offsets_m: every in-plane voxel with density > 0 is a column of 105 isochromats at (x_m[ix], y_m[iy], z_offsets_m[n]) uniformly spaced at 0.1 mm over -5.25 mm < z < 5.25 mm (three slice thicknesses, so slice profiles are simulated), each carrying density/105 and the voxel's T1, T2, B0; no sub-voxel spread in x or y; magnetization starts at thermal equilibrium; noise-free

endpoint: complex image on the 18x18 [y,x] grid and, per vial, the median magnitude over the vial voxels that do not touch another label divided by the same quantity for label 1
bloch_simulation: simulate the exported sequence.seq file itself with an established Bloch simulator (KomaMRI is the reference implementation; MRzero is acceptable); do not replace it with your own Bloch or EPG code

simulation_output_schema.raw_signal: complex [18 acquired echoes, 18 samples] in chronological order, after ADC phase demodulation, before any reconstruction; encoding convention exp(-2 pi i (kx x + ky y)); an arbitrary single global receiver phase is accepted
simulation_output_schema.kxy_cycles_per_m: float [18,18,2] k-space position [kx, ky] of every sample computed from the exported sequence
simulation_output_schema.echo_index: int [18] echo number (1..9) within its train of every acquired echo
simulation_output_schema.shot_index: int [18] acquired shot number (1..2) of every acquired echo
simulation_output_schema.phantom_sha256: SHA256 of the phantom file used

reconstruct_cli: python reconstruct.py --input simulation.npz --output image.npz. Standalone: helper code inside this one file, installed third-party imports allowed; it must work in a clean directory containing only this file and the archive, using only the archive contents. It will be rerun on archives with the same keys whose raw_signal comes from a different object acquired with your sequence.

image_output_schema.image: complex [18,18] on the [y,x] grid of the phantom (row index increases with y, column with x), no flips or shifts

report_output_schema.realized_effective_echo_time_ms: float measured from the exported sequence
report_output_schema.realized_echo_spacing_ms: float measured from the exported sequence
report_output_schema.realized_flip_angles_deg: {"excitation": float, "refocusing": float} measured from the exported sequence
report_output_schema.echo_train_design: string: how the echo train meets the echo-train requirement
report_output_schema.signal_ratio_by_label: object mapping each vial label to the endpoint ratio measured on your image

acceptance: all of the requirements above, checked on the exported file, on its replay for test columns, and on the public and a hidden object (different geometry, T1 and T2 within the stated ranges) acquired with your sequence; your reconstruct.py output on the hidden measurement must match a reference reconstruction of the same data (normalized RMS difference of magnitudes after a least-squares scale at most 3%)
grading_note: The grader reads the exported sequence back, checks limits, rasters, flip angles, slice selection, timing and the sampling contract, replays it in KomaMRI on the public object, a hidden object and test columns, compares your simulated signal with the replay, and reruns reconstruct.py on the hidden measurements.
